experiment: DETR layout detection for page classification
status: FAILED — not viable in Claude container or Cloud Run 4vCPU

attempts.result: OOM — torch + CUDA packages exceed 4GB container memory
Model weight mismatch — transformers 5.5.3 renames all DETR weights (prefix mismatch), model loads with random weights, zero detections on all pages. ~7s/page on CPU.
Timeout — HuggingFace cache migration + model loading exceeds container time limit

root_causes: PDFs are scanned images (1728x2312 PNG per page, zero text layer) — text-based classification impossible
DETR ResNet-101 backbone + transformer is ~170MB weights, ~800MB+ in memory during inference
CPU inference ~7s/page × 62 pages = 7+ minutes, exceeds container timeout
transformers v5.x changed DETR weight naming convention, breaking compatibility with cmarkea checkpoint

alternative_tried.result: 0% accuracy — pages have zero text layer, all classified as 'annet'
alternative_tried.conclusion: Confirms these PDFs require vision-based or OCR-based classification

pdf_structure.format: Each page is a single embedded PNG image (1728x2312, ~35-50KB per image)
pdf_structure.text_layer: None — scanned documents with no OCR text embedded

conclusion: Gemini classify_pdf() at $0.0003/entity remains the only viable page classifier for these scanned PDFs. DETR could work on a machine with 8GB+ RAM and 10+ minutes, but provides no advantage over Gemini at that point. For Cloud Run production deployment, Gemini manifest classification should be the first call before extraction.
recommendation: Drop DETR from the pipeline. The Gemini manifest experiment already proved that classify_pdf prevents the most dangerous error (hallucinated company values). At $0.0003/entity it's 25% cost increase on a $0.0012 extraction — negligible. No free local alternative exists for image-only PDFs at reasonable latency.
